children: The Rs 1,000-crore Hero Motors IPO receives bids for 6.66 times the shares on offer during its subscription period

Shares of Hero Motors rebounded sharply on Wednesday after making a weak debut on the stock exchanges, rising nearly 19 per cent from the opening price as heavy trading volumes drove the stock above its initial public offering (IPO) price.

The stock climbed to an intraday high of Rs 97.84 on the BSE, up 19.17 per cent from its opening price of Rs 82.10. On the NSE, it also touched Rs 97.84, representing a gain of 16.17 per cent from its issue price of Rs 84.

The sharp recovery came despite the stock listing at a discount to its IPO price. Hero Motors opened at Rs 82 on the NSE, a 2.38 per cent discount to the issue price, while the BSE opening price of Rs 82.10 represented a 2.26 per cent discount.
The stock’s recovery also pushed it above the IPO price during the session, reversing the initial weakness seen at listing.
The Rs 1,000-crore Hero Motors IPO received bids for 6.66 times the shares on offer during its subscription period from September 16 to September 18. The allotment was finalised on September 21.

Demand was strongest among non-institutional investors (NIIs), whose portion was subscribed 9.86 times. The retail portion was subscribed 8.23 times, while the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category received bids for 1.49 times the shares reserved for it.
The book-built issue comprised a fresh issue of 7.14 crore shares worth Rs 600 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.76 crore shares amounting to Rs 400 crore.

The IPO had a lot size of 178 shares, requiring retail investors to commit Rs 14,952 at the upper end of the price band. ICICI Securities was the book-running lead manager, while Kfin Technologies was the registrar.

Hero Motors, incorporated in April 1998, develops and manufactures powertrain solutions for automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across markets including the US, Europe, India and Southeast Asia.

Its portfolio covers electric and conventional powertrains for two-wheelers, e-bikes, performance and off-road vehicles, electric and hybrid cars, heavy-duty vehicles and electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) applications.

The company provides both system-level and component-level solutions across product design, prototyping, validation, development and manufacturing. Its capabilities include continuously variable transmissions (CVTs), electric vehicle transmissions, electric motors, integrated drive units and gear sets. Hero Motors also operates in the global e-bike powertrain market.

Hero Motors counts companies including BMW, Ducati, enviolo, Formula Motorsport, Hummingbird EV and HWA among its global customers. The company has also highlighted its in-house engineering capabilities and partnerships as part of its technology and product development strategy.
